findings.title: Mandatory CapabilityRegistry route has no containment-preservation or explicit incompatibility contract

nativeEvidence.fact: ToolDescriptor.sandbox is the native optional declaration of required containment; absent/NONE skips the gate.
normalizeRegistration normalizes descriptor; the constructed normalized descriptor omits sandbox without rejecting its presence.
The actual normalized descriptors determine compositionFingerprint and are spread into the executable ToolDefinition.
enforceSandbox runs in the common pipeline but requiredSandboxMode maps missing sandbox to NONE and returns before evaluating the configured gate.

findings.invariant: A reviewed requirement for containment must remain effective through the mandatory managed composition path, or that capability must be rejected as incompatible before activation/publication. A capability cannot silently weaken the fixed security control.
findings.permittedCounterexample: A trusted catalog entry supplies an otherwise valid reviewed tool registration with sandbox WORKSPACE (equivalently EGRESS), correct nativeProviderVersion/config/artifact/target binding, and ordinary policy/approval permission. Its activation constructs the required CapabilityRegistry and provides that registry. The current normalizer drops sandbox; the resulting descriptors still satisfy the explicitly listed provider/tool identity checks. A builder preserving the current adapter as instructed and implementing only those checks can publish it. At dispatch the native sandbox port may even be present and deny every request, but requiredSandboxMode sees no sandbox field and returns NONE, so the gate is not called before the body. This requires neither hostile code nor control-service replacement.
findings.whyCandidateDefect: The spec newly mandates this exact adapter for every managed tool (119), explicitly protects the sandbox control (36), but has no rule to preserve this security declaration or to reject unsupported containment requirements before normalization. Correct provider binding/fingerprint hashes the already lossy descriptor; it cannot restore containment. General descriptor/catalog correspondence is not an exact pre/post security-field rule, especially once the public registry has discarded the field. This is an unresolved composition compatibility contract, not a demand to implement the proposed lifecycle now or to add new native isolation.
findings.smallestNormativeCorrection: For this foundation, explicitly limit compatible managed tools to reviewed sandbox absent/NONE. Require the trusted catalog to retain each tool containment requirement independently of the normalized registry and reject any non-NONE requirement before activate; reject a mismatch or stripped security declaration instead of treating absence after normalization as NONE. Alternatively specify a concrete preservation/validation path through normalized descriptors, fingerprint and executable ToolDefinition, with compatibility impact explicitly reviewed. Do not silently modify a fingerprinted descriptor after registration. Keep unsupported contained tools and stronger isolation in the original backlog; this restriction is not a parity waiver.
findings.futureProof: Extend ML03 with a synthetic reviewed WORKSPACE/EGRESS registration through the actual public managed factory and actual CapabilityRegistry: either reject before activate with zero body calls, or preserve the mode through publication and show a missing/denying gate prevents body invocation. Check the normalized fingerprinted descriptor and descriptor received by the native gate. Also retain the supported NONE positive path. NOT_RUN.
